title: page.look reads a style at the viewport an agent names ("390x844", "phone", "tablet", "1440x900") and answers an element it holds but hides with hidden: display:none, not STYLE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND
steps: S1: From packages/tools/tracy-site-tools in the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap test/look-style.test.mjs
S2: Read the exit code, the `# pass`, `# fail`, `# skipped` and `# cancelled` lines and the tests named below.
expect: S1 exits 0 with 0 failures, 0 skipped, 0 cancelled.

'viewportOf: a name, a device word or a size, each read at the viewport of its width class' passes: `390x844`, `phone 390×844` and `phone` read as mobile, `tablet` and `768x1024` as tablet (768×1024), `1440x900` and `1280x900` as desktop; `sideways` is still BAD_STYLE.

'🔒 findTarget + describeTarget: an element hidden on this viewport is found by its exact words and said hidden, not "not found"' passes: the words of a button under a `display:none` wrapper find it, `hidden` is `display:none on <div.wtb-actions>`, a partial match never reaches a hidden element, and styleAnswer carries the reason.
'BROWSER_SCRIPT (style): a tablet read at 768×1024…' passes: Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride gets width 768, height 1024, mobile true.
evidence: Flow D 05/10/2026: WordPress hide-mobile `viewport:"phone 390×844"` → BAD_STYLE then STYLE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND for the button it had just hidden; Joomla hide-mobile `"390x844"` and `"1440x900"` → BAD_STYLE ×2 (maxSameRefusal failed), then STYLE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND; EmDash hide-mobile `"390x844"`, `"1280x900"` → BAD_STYLE ×2, then STYLE_TARGET_NOT_FOUND.
fence: Mechanism only, no stand: findTarget and describeTarget run on a small fake page under node's vm, the browser script against a scripted CDP. Not covered: a real Chromium's layout (box sizes, innerText) on the three templates.
